cases.name: Viridiana “Viri" Arevalo
cases.about: According to family members, she was religious, loved to draw comics, and was looking forward to being a mother.
cases.relationship: Brother / stepbrother / partner or sibling's brother / brother-in-law
cases.narrative: He strangled her from behind while she was sitting on the couch in the living room of the family’s house. He then made sure she stayed dead by wrapping her head in black duct tape, picked her body up, put it in the trunk of his car, and dumped her in a field some 40 miles away near Whitewright in Fannin County. A few days after the slaying, Eduardo Arevalo would pick up his sister’s body from the field and then dump her again. This time within the city limits – because he wanted his family to find her – in an alleyway on Strickland Avenue. After that, he stopped at a nearby Whataburger, and then he went back home. Neighbors found the pregnant woman’s body behind their own homes on 12/22/2019.
